prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling through ligand design

statement.case_for: I have moved from B053 to B011. The round-1 exchange showed me what I had already admitted in my own case against: B053 has one explicit supporter, and a prize cannot rest on one member's field proximity. B011 is the candidacy where the mechanism, the credit and the maturity can all be stated and checked. Amine binding, deprotonation and C-N reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes were worked out by Hartwig and Buchwald in parallel, and the successive bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphine ligand generations were designed from that mechanistic understanding. That is what turned a harsh, substrate-limited reaction into a general one. More than 25 years of independent confirmation and daily use in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis mean there is no maturity question. A two-name citation is clean, and four members prefer it with identical names. Novelty relative to 2010: Heck, Negishi and Suzuki honoured C-C bond formation, whereas this is a different bond with a different catalytic cycle and a ligand-design solution to a different rate-limiting step. The citation should say carbon-nitrogen and ligand design explicitly to keep the two prizes apart.
statement.case_against: The 2010 overlap is a real concern and the committee should not wave it away: some members will read this as a heteroatom extension of already honoured palladium chemistry. Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a genuine precursor, and I would like the expert reports to show how far it was from a general method. I also give up what I value most in B053, a physical mechanism for biological energy conversion, and B011 is a synthetic-methods prize in which my own expertise gives me little independent leverage, so I rely on the expert reports and on Somfai, Aqvist and Zou. Finally, B068 has the widest opening base, and if its credit were settled and a degrader approved I would take it much more seriously.

responses.point: Aili asks what B053 has enabled beyond its explanatory value, and holds that crowded credit in B068 does not lower its scientific rank.
responses.response: The question is fair. Protein electron tunnelling mostly enabled understanding: it is the framework used to reason about respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes and to design redox proteins, but it did not give chemists a new tool in the way B011 or B068 did. I cannot answer your test convincingly, and that is part of why I am leaving B053. On B068 I accept your point that many claimants show a large, reproduced field, but for a prize the claimants must be cut to three. The PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands still look like two discoveries, and your own file concedes the cut is contested. My view of B068 as a next-year candidate stands, unless the chair's questions produce a single citation that Handa or Ciulli can sit beside Crews and Deshaies in.

responses.point: Sparr doubts B053 can win a majority since nobody else ranked it, and asks whether I would pair it with something instead of pushing it alone.
responses.response: You are right, and I answer by moving, not by pairing. A two-part prize with B053 would carry Gray, Winkler and at least one name from the other part, and no member has shown me that the pairing would persuade a fifth voter. I also share your reservation about condensates for a different reason from yours: I would want to see which observations in cells are beyond dispute before the committee writes a physical principle into a citation. That is a timing concern, not a rejection of B019.

responses.point: Zou proposes B011 plus nitrogenase structure credited to Rees alone, and asks how Einsle and Seefeldt should be weighed if three slots are forced.
responses.response: I cannot support the two-part configuration. If the nitrogenase part is to rest on structure, as you argue, then Einsle's high-resolution carbide structure is part of the credit, and Rees alone is an incomplete roster that invites the objection you list yourself. Adding Einsle gives four people with B011. Dropping a C-N coupling laureate to make room breaks a clean two-name attribution. Between Einsle and Seefeldt I would take Einsle for a structure-based citation, but my answer is that this is a reason to keep B003 as a standalone later candidate once the N2-binding site is resolved, not to attach it to B011 now.

responses.point: Somfai calls Buchwald and Hartwig the cleanest attribution on the list, with Kosugi only a narrower precursor.
responses.response: I accept that and my round-1 hesitation is mostly answered by the chair's summary. Every member who addresses Kosugi would put him in the background narrative. I would still ask that the expert report state what the tin-amide chemistry lacked (scope, catalyst loading, base and ligand control), so the committee's reasoning on priority is on the record. I also agree with your point that B011 should be argued from the mechanism of the catalytic cycle and not from usage statistics.

responses.point: Linke asks supporters of B011 for a single reason it differs from the 2010 prize, and for whether Kosugi belongs in the citation.
responses.response: My one-sentence answer: 2010 honoured catalysts that join carbon to carbon through transmetalation, whereas C-N coupling needed new ligand design to make the amido-palladium intermediate undergo C-N reductive elimination, a different bottleneck. The citation should name carbon-nitrogen bond formation and ligand design explicitly. Kosugi should stay in the background narrative, since his reaction used toxic tin amides and was narrow, which makes the general method the achievement of Buchwald and Hartwig.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports show the tin-amide precedent of Kosugi to be a narrow reaction, which I assume but have not seen documented.
Whether the committee will accept that C-N coupling is a distinct achievement from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or will find the overlap decisive.
Whether B068 can settle one citation (Handa or Ciulli beside Crews and Deshaies) soon enough to overtake B011 in this round.
Whether my move away from B053 is read as support for B011 by others in a way that hides the weaker field-specific evidence I have not independently assessed.
statement.conflict_note: My cytochrome c oxidase electron and proton transfer work is close to B053, which I no longer prefer, so that proximity no longer bears on my position. I have no apparent tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, as before, and I do not see a required recusal.
